answer: Latent-capacity escrow. Each new identity must pre-fund a lotus of verifiable compute reserved for future audits; the reserve is locked, non-transferable, and released only after sustained honest work. The dune of accumulated reserves raises an attacker's per-clone cost above expected clone yield. An onyx ledger records reserve depletion against each identity. Violating identities forfeit reserves, and cloning requires re-funding fresh capacity, so marginal clones lose value.
